figures.source_locator: document.xml paragraphs 78-81; connector paragraphs 79 (2 strokes) and 80 (2 strokes)
figures.caption: Substitution method, Example 1 (2x + 3y = 5, 3x + y = 4), step 4, recovered from the school note with its fractions and the four cancellation strokes. Printed line 3 is a source slip (see notes).
figures.alt_text: Working for step 4 of substitution Example 1. Printed lines: 2x + 12 - 9x = 5; 12 - 7x = 5; 12 - 5 - 7x = 10; then the fractions 7 over 7 equals 7x over 7, with a short diagonal cancellation stroke through the 7 above and the 7 below in each fraction (four strokes, cancelling the 7s); then x = 1. The printed line 12 - 5 - 7x = 10 does not follow from 12 - 7x = 5; moving terms gives 12 - 5 = 7x, that is 7 = 7x.
figures.notes: Four strokes (two anchored in paragraph 79, two in 80) are drawn through the 7 above and the 7 below in each fraction: cancelling 7/7 and 7x/7 gives 1 = x, consistent with x = 1 (12 - 7(1) = 5). Stroke positions are as drawn by LibreOffice; Word placement was not viewed. Source slip kept, not edited: printed line 12 - 5 - 7x = 10 is false for x = 1 (it gives 0 = 10); 12 - 5 = 7x was probably meant. Paragraph 83 holds one further stroke over the words 'Step 5': it sits on a heading, beside no equation, so no operation is supported and it is not reproduced.

figures.source_locator: document.xml paragraphs 110-120 (fractions); connector paragraph 111 (one stroke, not reproduced)
figures.caption: Substitution method, Example 2 (4m - 3n = 0, m + 2n = 3), steps 4 and 5, with the fractions the importer lost. One stray source stroke whose target cannot be determined is not shown. Printed fraction line 3/11 - 24/1 is a source slip (see notes).
figures.alt_text: Working for steps 4 and 5 of substitution Example 2. 12 - 8n - 3n = 0; 12 - 11n = 0; minus 11n over minus 11 equals minus 12 over minus 11; n = 1 and 1 over 11. Step 5: substitute n = 12 over 11 into equation 3: m = 3 - 2 times 12 over 11; m = 3 over 1 minus 24 over 11; then 3 over 11 minus 24 over 1 equals 9 over 11 as printed; Hence m = 9 over 11 and n = 12 over 11.
figures.notes: Fractions recovered from Office Math: -11n/-11 = -12/-11 gives n = 12/11 = 1 1/11 (as printed); m = 3 - 2(12/11) = 3/1 - 24/11 = 9/11. Source slip kept, not edited: the line 3/11 - 24/1 = 9/11 has its denominators misplaced (3 - 24/11 = 33/11 - 24/11 = 9/11); the result is right. Paragraph 111 holds one stroke anchored 152.7 pt below its line, so it lands on a different line in different renderers and over no term in LibreOffice (it crosses the word 'Substitute'). Its target is ambiguous, so no operation is asserted and the stroke is omitted from the scratch render only.
